key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2-NiCr coatings than conventional APS, but this does not translate into better high-angle erosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical coatings, axial powder feeding in HV-APS is a practical route to improve hardness and sliding wear performance, while erosion performance may remain unchanged under severe impact conditions.
method: Compared conventional APS with radial powder injection vs. supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding
Evaluated coating porosity, microhardness, phase composition, erosion, and ball-on-disc wear
Used Cr3C2-NiCr (Metco 5241) coatings deposited on S235 steel substrates
evidence_signal: HV-APS reduced porosity from 11.99% to 6.16% and raised microhardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, while lowering wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3; erosion rates at 90° were nearly identical (0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g).
watch_item: The improved microstructure and tribological response may not generalize to erosion-dominated service, especially at high impact angles where damage mechanisms were similar.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
